analysis:
Examined the head text of ProviderLoop+InferenceHandler.swift (lines 619-1569) and the two patches. Changes in this file: lines 135 and 513 swap autopilotAllowsModel for autopilotServesModel in the admission gate (throwIfRefusingNewLocalWork and the authoritative post-suspension check). In ProviderLoop+MTPUpgrade.swift, the patch adds transitionGenerations.begin(.modelLoading) after isLoadingAny = true (line 127). Neither the definition of autopilotServesModel nor the matching end() for the new begin() call is in the supplied evidence.

The visible part of the inference task preserves the existing controls. Encryption failure is fail-closed: emitSSE and the key setup send an encryption_failure terminal, never plaintext. Chunks are sealed with the per-request precomputed shared key (T-008). Cancellation maps to 499 with partial settle. The cache scope comes from remoteCache.scope, which is coordinator-authored, and cache results are emitted only when a scope exists (T-041). The Super owner path passes remoteCache.scope. Template-failure logs omit prompt content, and only normalized reasons go on the wire. The response hash covers content, reasoning and tool calls. Nothing in the visible region appears to change; the relevant behavior was unchanged context.

Open integration questions, not findings: (1) whether autopilotServesModel is at least as strict as autopilotAllowsModel, i.e. it does not admit network work for models the operator or autopilot has not selected; (2) whether every exit path of the MTP upgrade load, including thrown errors and early returns after line 127, pairs the new transitionGenerations.begin(.modelLoading) with an end. An unpaired begin could permanently stall generation-gated transitions and cause availability loss or stale-state issues. The defer blocks visible in the patch handle only isLoadingAny and deviceActivity. I cannot verify the rest from the supplied evidence.
